## LegatorOCR 0.2.0-pre.75 — Markdown, CBZ, own word lists, fewer false tables

(0.2.0-pre.74 was published on GitHub without files; this version is the same code with the finished documentation and the re-shot window clips, built for Linux, macOS and Windows.)

Compared with ScanTailor Advanced, OCRmyPDF, NAPS2 and K2pdfopt; these are the gaps that could be closed cleanly.

### Added
- **`--markdown FILE.md`** (with `--ocr`): headings as `##`, tables as pipe tables, columns read one after the other, `<!-- page N -->` before every page, pictures marked `*[figure]*`. Recognised text never turns into Markdown structure (`#`, `1.`, `*`, `|` are escaped).
- **`--cbz FILE.cbz`** (with `--format png` or `jpeg`): the processed pages as a comic-book archive (ZIP in reading order) for e-readers and comic viewers.
- **`--user-words FILE`, `--user-patterns FILE`** (Tesseract): names, terms and code shapes of the book. The OCR cache keys on the content of both files, so changing a list never returns old results. The native engine ignores them.
- **Shooting rhythm: retakes that were deleted.** With a regular timer rhythm (most gaps on one value), a gap that is a multiple of it between two kept frames counts as shots taken and deleted. On the 120-frame `macromedia` session: 15 shots at a 10 s timer, so the suggested timer rises from 10 s to 13 s.

### Repaired
- **False tables in Word/EPUB/Excel**: lines of text next to a picture whose OCR noise (`~`, `u`, `|`) lined up like a second column were turned into tables. A table now needs real words (or digits) in at least 80 % of its cells and in every column. On the first 40 sheets of `macromedia` the tables dropped from about 28 (extrapolated from the full run) to 7; the book has no real tables, the unit test checks that real two-column tables stay.

Built and tested by the CI of this release.

Speed: the per-pixel loops of sharpening, denoising, deblurring, paper whitening and the grey conversion now run on all cores. Output is byte-identical (checked on six pages with every cleanup option on); on a 2-core machine the time did not change measurably, the gain shows with more cores. The `--timings` profile has finer stages (`page/prepare`, `page/render`, `output/colour-window`).

Presentation film of the new options (39 s, real output, 8 subtitle languages): `docs/video/noutati.mp4`, made by `scripts/make-novelty-film.py`.

Documentation: README in 8 languages, the 8 guide PDFs and the presentation page describe the new options.  All 11 window clips (`docs/video/gui`) were re-shot with this version by scripts (`scripts/gui-clips`); `docs/audit/competitors.md` and `COMPARISON.md` were re-checked on 2026-11-25 (ScanTailor Spectre added).
